correctness.rationale: Starting from the frozen exact quartic Bloch condition, solving linearly for \(Q=\cos\theta_1+\cos\theta_2\) is legitimate away from \(k=N_n\), and spectral membership is exactly \(|Q(k)|\le2\). With \(k=N_n+x/N_n\) and \(y=\ell x\), direct dominant-balance expansion gives \(Q=(-1)^n(\sin(2\mu)y/2-2\sin(2\mu)/y-2\cos(2\mu))+O(N_n^{-2})\). The limiting quotient is strictly increasing on each half-line; its four simple crossings with \(\pm2\) are exactly the submitted half-angle expressions. The central point is nonspectral, so the two half-line allowed intervals remain separated for large \(n\). Squaring \(k\) doubles the limiting momentum shifts and leaves an \(O(n^{-2})\) energy-edge error. A fresh symbolic leading-order expansion in this audit reproduced the singular \(-2\sin(2\mu)/y\) term; the frozen verifier independently checks the four edges and second-order convergence at several parameter values.
correctness.risk: The theorem is for fixed interior \(\mu\); the asymptotics are nonuniform as \(\mu\to0\) or \(\mu\to\pi/2\).

final_claim: For the phase-rotated square quantum graph with \(U=e^{i\mu}R\), \(0<\mu<\pi/2\), and common edge length \(\ell\), the spectrum in an \(O(N_n^{-1})\) momentum window around \(N_n=n\pi/\ell\) consists asymptotically of exactly two bands, whose four energy-edge shifts converge to the stated \(\sec\mu\), \(\tan(\mu/2)\), and \(\cot(\mu/2)\) constants with \(O(n^{-2})\) error.
limitations: No uniform claim as the phase approaches either endpoint.
